segments.name: Merchant
segments.description: Accepts card and cash payments, and provides point-of-sale software, cash management and lending to community and corporate merchants across Southern Africa.
segments.evidence: Our merchant solutions serve merchants of all sizes, helping them accept payments, manage and digitize cash, run their operations and access working capital.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.description: Provides transactional accounts, lending and insurance to underserviced consumers, principally social welfare grant recipients in South Africa.
segments.evidence: Consumer, which provides banking, lending and insurance solutions to consumers, principally recipients of social welfare grants in South Africa

segments.name: Enterprise
segments.description: Connects enterprises to consumers and businesses through payment processing, prepaid solutions and bill payment infrastructure.
segments.evidence: Enterprise, which provides payment processing, prepaid solutions and bill payment infrastructure connecting enterprises to consumers and businesses.

revenueModel.text: Merchants, consumers and enterprises pay transaction-based fees, ad valorem charges, account and lending interest, insurance premiums and software and hardware fees.
revenueModel.evidence: Merchant Revenues in Merchant are derived from a combination of transaction-based fees and an ad valorem pricing model.

changes.text: In fiscal 2026 the group decided to exit its ATM business, concluding it was structurally loss-making and immaterial in scale.
changes.evidence: In the third quarter, we made the decision to exit our ATM business, which we had concluded was structurally loss-making and immaterial in scale, recognizing an impairment and once-off costs of approximately ZAR 27 million in connection with the wind-down.

changes.text: In fiscal 2026 the group sunset SwitchPay, a legacy buy-now-pay-later product.
changes.evidence: In the same quarter, we sunset SwitchPay Proprietary Limited ("SwitchPay"), a legacy buy-now-pay-later product, recognizing an impairment of $0.4 million (ZAR 6.5 million).

changes.text: In fiscal 2026 the group disposed of its remaining stake in Cell-C as part of simplifying the group.
changes.evidence: Earlier in fiscal 2026, we finalized the liquidation of CPS, releasing provisions of ZAR 65 million, and disposed of our remaining stake in Cell-C for proceeds of $3.9 million (ZAR 50 million).
